c1-bioetika-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Why Germline Editing Is Different
c1-bioetika-01.scenario: A discussion group on medical ethics is talking about gene editing.
c1-bioetika-01.prompt: Say why changing the germline is more controversial than treating one patient.
cues: Say that the change is heritable
c1-bioetika-01.target: A csíravonal-módosítás örökíthető, ezért az utódokat is érinti.
c1-bioetika-01.english: Germline modification is heritable, so it also affects the descendants.
c1-bioetika-01.canDo: I can explain why changing the germline is more controversial than treating one patient.

c1-bioetika-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Presumed Consent
c1-bioetika-02.scenario: A discussion group on medical ethics is talking about organ donation.
c1-bioetika-02.prompt: Explain what presumed consent means in Hungary.
cues: Say who counts as a donor
c1-bioetika-02.target: A feltételezett beleegyezés azt jelenti, hogy az elhunyt donor, hacsak életében nem tiltakozott.
c1-bioetika-02.english: Presumed consent means that the deceased is a donor unless they objected in life.
c1-bioetika-02.canDo: I can explain what presumed consent means in organ donation (*feltételezett beleegyezés*).

c1-bioetika-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Two Views of the Embryo
c1-bioetika-03.scenario: A discussion group on medical ethics is talking about stem cell research.
c1-bioetika-03.prompt: Set out the two views on the moral status of the embryo.
cues: Give the view that dignity starts at conception
c1-bioetika-03.target: Az egyik nézet szerint a méltóság a fogantatással kezdődik, a másik szerint a morális státusz fokozatosan fejlődik ki.
c1-bioetika-03.english: According to one view dignity begins at conception, according to the other the moral status develops gradually.
c1-bioetika-03.canDo: I can set out two views on the moral status of the embryo (*embrió erkölcsi státusza*).

c1-bioetika-04.title: Communicative Challenge: The Karsai Case
c1-bioetika-04.scenario: A discussion group on medical ethics is talking about the Karsai case.
c1-bioetika-04.prompt: Say who Dániel Karsai was and what he asked the court in Strasbourg.
cues: Say which right he relied on
c1-bioetika-04.target: Karsai Dániel alkotmányjogász volt, és a strasbourgi bíróságon a magánélet tiszteletben tartásához való jogra hivatkozott.
c1-bioetika-04.english: Dániel Karsai was a constitutional lawyer, and at the Strasbourg court he relied on the right to respect for private life.
c1-bioetika-04.canDo: I can describe the Karsai case and the question it raised about dying with dignity.

c1-bioetika-05.title: Communicative Challenge: AI in Diagnosis
c1-bioetika-05.scenario: A discussion group on medical ethics is talking about AI in hospitals.
c1-bioetika-05.prompt: Say what AI changes in diagnosis and what the doctor still does.
cues: Say what the algorithm does quickly
Say what the doctor still does
c1-bioetika-05.target: Az algoritmus gyorsan áttekinti a felvételeket, de a beteggel az orvos beszél, empátiával.
c1-bioetika-05.english: The algorithm looks through the images quickly, but the doctor talks to the patient, with empathy.
c1-bioetika-05.canDo: I can discuss what AI changes in diagnosis and what the doctor still does.

c1-bioetika-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Dilemmas of the Unit
c1-bioetika-consolidation.scenario: A discussion group on medical ethics sums up the unit.
c1-bioetika-consolidation.prompt: Name one dilemma from this unit and say why it is hard.
c1-bioetika-consolidation.target: A fagyasztott embriók sorsa nehéz kérdés, mert a vágyott gyermek és az embrió méltósága ütközik.
c1-bioetika-consolidation.english: The fate of frozen embryos is a hard question, because the wished-for child and the dignity of the embryo clash.
c1-bioetika-consolidation.canDo: I can talk about the main dilemmas of this unit: gene editing, organ donation, the embryo, dying with dignity and AI in medicine.

c1-szerzodesek-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Before the Takeover
c1-szerzodesek-01.scenario: In a meeting about a company takeover, the talk turns to due diligence.
c1-szerzodesek-01.prompt: Say what the buyer checks before buying a company.
cues: Say what the buyer wants to know
c1-szerzodesek-01.target: A vevő jogi átvilágítást kér, mert tudni akarja, milyen kockázatok vannak a cégben.
c1-szerzodesek-01.english: The buyer asks for legal due diligence, because he wants to know what risks the company has.
c1-szerzodesek-01.canDo: I can talk about a company takeover: due diligence, warranties and the purchase agreement.

c1-szerzodesek-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Investor and Founders
c1-szerzodesek-02.scenario: In a meeting about a startup, the talk turns to the investor's terms.
c1-szerzodesek-02.prompt: Explain what liquidation preference means for the investor.
c1-szerzodesek-02.target: A likvidációs preferencia azt jelenti, hogy a cég eladásakor a befektető az alapítók előtt jut a pénzéhez.
c1-szerzodesek-02.english: Liquidation preference means that when the company is sold the investor gets his money before the founders.
c1-szerzodesek-02.canDo: I can explain the main terms of a venture capital deal (*kockázati tőke*, *likvidációs preferencia*).

c1-szerzodesek-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Cartels and Leniency
c1-szerzodesek-03.scenario: In a discussion of competition law, the talk turns to cartels.
c1-szerzodesek-03.prompt: Say what the cartel ban forbids and how leniency works.
cues: Say what competitors may not agree on
Say who can be exempt from the fine
c1-szerzodesek-03.target: A kartelltilalom tiltja az árrögzítő megállapodást, az engedékenységi politika pedig mentességet adhat az elsőként jelentkező cégnek.
c1-szerzodesek-03.english: The cartel ban forbids price-fixing agreements, and the leniency policy can give an exemption to the company that comes forward first.
c1-szerzodesek-03.canDo: I can explain what the cartel ban and the leniency policy are (*kartelltilalom*, *engedékenységi politika*).

c1-szerzodesek-04.title: Communicative Challenge: A Bidder Complains
c1-szerzodesek-04.scenario: In a discussion of public tenders, the talk turns to a bidder who feels unfairly excluded.
c1-szerzodesek-04.prompt: Say where a bidder can seek a remedy.
cues: Say what the body can do
c1-szerzodesek-04.target: A pályázó a Közbeszerzési Döntőbizottsághoz fordulhat, amely felfüggesztheti az eljárást.
c1-szerzodesek-04.english: The bidder can turn to the Public Procurement Arbitration Board, which can suspend the procedure.
c1-szerzodesek-04.canDo: I can explain how a bidder can seek a remedy in public procurement (*jogorvoslat*).

c1-szerzodesek-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Choosing the Law
c1-szerzodesek-05.scenario: In a discussion of a contract between firms in different EU countries, the talk turns to the governing law.
c1-szerzodesek-05.prompt: Say what the parties can agree on in the contract.
c1-szerzodesek-05.target: A felek a szerződésben kiköthetik a magyar jogot, és választottbíróságot is kijelölhetnek.
c1-szerzodesek-05.english: In the contract the parties can stipulate Hungarian law, and they can also appoint an arbitration court.
c1-szerzodesek-05.canDo: I can explain how parties choose the governing law and an arbitration court (*jogválasztás*, *választottbíróság*).

c1-szerzodesek-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Topics of the Unit
c1-szerzodesek-consolidation.scenario: In a discussion of corporate law, someone asks what the unit covered.
c1-szerzodesek-consolidation.prompt: Name two topics of this unit and say what each is about.
c1-szerzodesek-consolidation.target: A kartelltilalom a versenyről szól, a közbeszerzés pedig arról, hogyan költik a közpénzt.
c1-szerzodesek-consolidation.english: The cartel ban is about competition, and public procurement is about how public money is spent.
c1-szerzodesek-consolidation.canDo: I can talk about the main topics of this unit: takeovers, venture capital, competition law, public procurement and arbitration.

c1-emberijogok-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Going to Strasbourg
c1-emberijogok-01.scenario: In a talk about human rights, the conversation turns to the Strasbourg Court.
c1-emberijogok-01.prompt: Say what a person must do before turning to the Strasbourg Court.
cues: Say what must be exhausted first
c1-emberijogok-01.target: Strasbourghoz csak az fordulhat, aki előbb kimerítette a hazai jogorvoslatokat.
c1-emberijogok-01.english: Only a person who has first exhausted the domestic remedies can turn to Strasbourg.
c1-emberijogok-01.canDo: I can explain what the European Convention on Human Rights and the Strasbourg Court do.

c1-emberijogok-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Minority Languages
c1-emberijogok-02.scenario: In a talk about the Carpathian Basin, the conversation turns to minority languages.
c1-emberijogok-02.target: A Regionális vagy Kisebbségi Nyelvek Európai Kartája a kisebbségi nyelveket védi.
c1-emberijogok-02.english: The European Charter for Regional or Minority Languages protects minority languages.
c1-emberijogok-02.canDo: I can explain what the European Charter for Regional or Minority Languages protects (*Regionális vagy Kisebbségi Nyelvek Európai Kartája*).

c1-emberijogok-03.title: Communicative Challenge: The Gyöngyöspata Case
c1-emberijogok-03.scenario: In a talk about school segregation, the conversation turns to the Gyöngyöspata case.
c1-emberijogok-03.prompt: Say what the Kúria decided about the Roma children.
c1-emberijogok-03.target: A Kúria megállapította, hogy a roma gyermekek elkülönítése jogellenes volt, és sérelemdíjat ítélt meg nekik.
c1-emberijogok-03.english: The Kúria found that the separation of the Roma children was unlawful, and it awarded them compensation.
c1-emberijogok-03.canDo: I can describe the Gyöngyöspata school case and what the Kúria decided.

c1-emberijogok-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Supported Decisions
c1-emberijogok-04.scenario: In a talk about disability rights, the conversation turns to legal capacity.
c1-emberijogok-04.target: A támogatott döntéshozatalnál a fogyatékossággal élő személy segítséggel maga dönt, és megtartja a cselekvőképességét.
c1-emberijogok-04.english: With supported decision-making the person with a disability decides himself with help, and keeps his legal capacity.
c1-emberijogok-04.canDo: I can explain what the UN disability convention (CRPD) changes for legal capacity and independent living.

c1-emberijogok-05.title: Communicative Challenge: The Paris Principles
c1-emberijogok-05.scenario: In a talk about human rights institutions, the conversation turns to independence.
c1-emberijogok-05.prompt: Say what the Paris Principles require of a national human rights institution.
c1-emberijogok-05.target: A Párizsi Elvek szerint a nemzeti emberi jogi intézménynek függetlennek kell lennie a kormánytól.
c1-emberijogok-05.english: According to the Paris Principles, a national human rights institution must be independent of the government.
c1-emberijogok-05.canDo: I can explain what the Paris Principles and the UN Universal Periodic Review are.

c1-emberijogok-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Topics of the Unit
c1-emberijogok-consolidation.scenario: In a talk about human rights, someone asks what the unit covered.
c1-emberijogok-consolidation.prompt: Name two topics of this unit and say what each is about.
c1-emberijogok-consolidation.target: A Karta a kisebbségi nyelveket védi, a Kúria pedig megállapította, hogy az iskolai elkülönítés jogellenes volt.
c1-emberijogok-consolidation.english: The Charter protects minority languages, and the Kúria found that school separation was unlawful.
c1-emberijogok-consolidation.canDo: I can talk about the main topics of this unit: the Strasbourg Court, minority languages, school segregation, disability rights and human rights monitoring.

c1-polgariengedetlenseg-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Passive Resistance
c1-polgariengedetlenseg-01.scenario: In a talk about Hungarian history, the conversation turns to passive resistance.
c1-polgariengedetlenseg-01.prompt: Say what passive resistance meant after 1849.
cues: Say what people refused to do
Say what they held on to
c1-polgariengedetlenseg-01.target: A passzív ellenállás azt jelentette, hogy az emberek nem vállaltak hivatalt, és ragaszkodtak az alkotmányhoz.
c1-polgariengedetlenseg-01.english: Passive resistance meant that people did not take office, and held on to the constitution.
c1-polgariengedetlenseg-01.canDo: I can explain what passive resistance was in the Deák era (*passzív rezisztencia, adómegtagadás*).

c1-polgariengedetlenseg-02.title: Communicative Challenge: The Beszélő Editors
c1-polgariengedetlenseg-02.scenario: In a talk about the 1980s, the conversation turns to samizdat.
c1-polgariengedetlenseg-02.prompt: Say what samizdat was and what the editors did.
c1-polgariengedetlenseg-02.target: A szamizdat tiltott, saját kiadású lap volt, a szerkesztők pedig a nevüket vállalták.
c1-polgariengedetlenseg-02.english: Samizdat was a banned, self-published paper, and the editors put their names to it.
c1-polgariengedetlenseg-02.canDo: I can say what samizdat was and why the Beszélő editors published under their names (*szamizdat, névvállalás*).

c1-polgariengedetlenseg-03.title: Communicative Challenge: The Taxi Blockade
c1-polgariengedetlenseg-03.scenario: In a talk about 1990, the conversation turns to the taxi blockade.
c1-polgariengedetlenseg-03.prompt: Say how the taxi blockade began and ended.
c1-polgariengedetlenseg-03.target: A blokád a benzináremeléssel kezdődött, és tárgyalásos megegyezéssel ért véget.
c1-polgariengedetlenseg-03.english: The blockade began with the petrol price rise, and ended with a negotiated agreement.
c1-polgariengedetlenseg-03.canDo: I can describe how the 1990 taxi blockade began and how it ended (*taxisblokád, Érdekegyeztető Tanács*).

c1-polgariengedetlenseg-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Teachers in 2022
c1-polgariengedetlenseg-04.scenario: In a talk about recent years, the conversation turns to the teachers' protest.
c1-polgariengedetlenseg-04.prompt: Say why some teachers chose civil disobedience.
c1-polgariengedetlenseg-04.target: A tanárok szerint a sztrájkjog korlátozása után a polgári engedetlenség maradt, ezért nem vették fel a munkát.
c1-polgariengedetlenseg-04.english: According to the teachers, after the restriction of the right to strike civil disobedience remained, so they did not take up work.
c1-polgariengedetlenseg-04.canDo: I can explain why some teachers chose civil disobedience in 2022 (*sztrájkjog, polgári engedetlenség*).

c1-polgariengedetlenseg-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Rawls on Disobedience
c1-polgariengedetlenseg-05.scenario: In a talk about political philosophy, the conversation turns to Rawls.
c1-polgariengedetlenseg-05.prompt: Say how Rawls defines civil disobedience.
cues: Say what kind of act it is
c1-polgariengedetlenseg-05.target: Rawls szerint a polgári engedetlenség nyilvános és erőszakmentes, és a tiltakozó vállalja a büntetést.
c1-polgariengedetlenseg-05.english: According to Rawls, civil disobedience is public and non-violent, and the protester accepts the punishment.
c1-polgariengedetlenseg-05.canDo: I can explain how Rawls defines civil disobedience.

c1-polgariengedetlenseg-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Topics of the Unit
c1-polgariengedetlenseg-consolidation.scenario: In a talk about civil disobedience, someone asks what the unit covered.
c1-polgariengedetlenseg-consolidation.prompt: Name two topics of this unit and say what each is about.
c1-polgariengedetlenseg-consolidation.target: A szamizdat tiltott lap volt, a taxisblokád pedig tárgyalással ért véget.
c1-polgariengedetlenseg-consolidation.english: Samizdat was a banned paper, and the taxi blockade ended with negotiation.
c1-polgariengedetlenseg-consolidation.canDo: I can talk about the main topics of this unit: passive resistance, samizdat, the taxi blockade, the teachers and Rawls.
